subskill: Overlap of a sliding window with a fixed solution set
prompt:
-21 < -5 - 2x ≤ 9
2k ≤ 5x - 8 < 2k + 19
In the system of inequalities above, k is a constant, and exactly two integers satisfy both inequalities. How much greater is the greatest possible integer value of k than the least possible integer value of k?
explanation: First inequality: adding 5 gives -16 < -2x ≤ 14, and dividing by -2 reverses both signs: 8 > x ≥ -7. So its integer solutions are -7, -6, ..., 7; the end -7 IS included (it came from ≤) and 8 is NOT. Second inequality: (2k + 8)/5 ≤ x < (2k + 27)/5, a window of length 19/5 = 3.8 that slides as k changes and always holds 3 or 4 integers. If the whole window sat inside -7, ..., 7 there would be at least 3 common integers, so exactly two happens only where the window hangs over an end of -7, ..., 7. Left end: the common integers must be -7 and -6, so -6 < (2k + 27)/5 ≤ -5 and (2k + 8)/5 ≤ -7, which give -28.5 < k ≤ -26: k = -28, -27, -26. Right end: the common integers must be 6 and 7, so 5 < (2k + 8)/5 ≤ 6 (and 7 is below the window's top), which gives 8.5 < k ≤ 11: k = 9, 10, 11. The greatest value is 11 and the least is -28, so the difference is 39. Choice 36 treats -7 as not a solution of the first inequality, which moves the left cluster to k = -25, -24. Choice 6 is the number of values of k, not the difference. Choice 2 finds only the right-end cluster (9 to 11) and misses the window hanging over the left end.
solve: const K=(ex,lo)=>{const ks=[]; for (let k=-300;k<=300;k++){ let n=0; for (let x=-150;x<=150;x++){ const t=-5-2*x; const P=(lo?-21<=t:-21<t)&&(ex?t<9:t<=9); const u=5*x-8; const Q=(2*k<=u)&&(u<2*k+19); if(P&&Q) n++; } if(n===2) ks.push(k);} return ks;}; const s=K(false,false); return s[s.length-1]-s[0];

mechanism: reverse the fixed inequality and keep the attained end x = -7
the second inequality is a window of fixed width sliding with k
exactly two common integers only where the window hangs over an end
take the greatest and least k across both ends
quantity_asked: the greatest possible integer k minus the least possible integer k for which exactly two integers satisfy both inequalities

setup.i: k in both ends of the second inequality of a system at the same rate (a sliding window of fixed width); the first inequality is a fixed compound
setup.ii: exactly two integers satisfy both inequalities
setup.iii: difference between the greatest and least integer values of k

plugback.why: The ask is a difference across two separate clusters of k; 39 cannot be substituted into either inequality, and checking it needs both clusters. Ascending order reaches the key only at try 4.

36.why: Dropping the attained end -7 shortens the fixed solution set on the left, which moves the left cluster of k; the stem does not show which way that moves the difference.

6.why: Answering the count of k values instead of the spread; whether a count exceeds or falls short of a spread depends on whether the values are consecutive, which the stem does not reveal.

2.why: Missing the left-end cluster; nothing in the stem says there are two places where the window can hang over.

counter_error.why: Treating -21 < ... as ≤ (so that 8 becomes a solution of the first inequality) moves the right cluster up to k = 12, 13 and gives 41, above the key and not an option.

far_distractor.why: Reporting the number of k values instead of their spread ordinarily overshoots by one (for consecutive values the count is the difference plus 1); here the values form two clusters far apart, so the count lands far below the spread.
